author: clean-loop9 SME critic (independent Claude critic subagent, 2026-11-19)

findings.claim: The new general residual statement is right in its main claim ('Any animation that changes the drawn size at some other moment can therefore go undetected'), but its explanatory clause before that claim mispredicts the outcome in three ways. The same wording is in the solved-run record's not-covered list (authoring/evidence/html-css-js/html-and-css/coding-lab-solved-run.json line 49 at 8135e3b5). Each case below was run on a fresh git archive of 598e61a2 with the private completed work plus one appended rule, through the full public suite, 3 runs each. The unmodified page was then opened in the pinned Chromium at 1280x1000 and sampled at about 0s and 1.5s and after scrolling. (a) 'its last keyframe if it fills forwards' is wrong as a description of the held value. After finish() a forwards-filled animation holds the value at the end of its final iteration. That value depends on the playback direction and the iteration count (Web Animations 4.9.1), not on which keyframe comes last. A 1s reverse forwards-filled animation on both tags whose last keyframe is identity and whose first keyframe is a reduced scale failed task 11 in 3 of 3 runs with the scaling message. A two-iteration alternate forwards-filled animation of the same shape also failed in 3 of 3. The wording predicts both would pass. The reverse case also hides a wrong page: a very long linear reverse forwards-filled animation from identity to a reduced scale passed all 12 in 3 of 3 runs. Its last keyframe is the reduced scale, so the wording predicts a failure. On the page, layout width and drawn width differ at every sample, with the computed scale near the reduced value. (b) 'it first finishes the finite animations on the checklist and the two tags' holds only for time-based animations. The test finishes an animation only when Number.isFinite(getComputedTiming().endTime). A scroll-driven animation runs one finite iteration, but its timing is progress-based and its end time is the percentage 100% (Web Animations 2 timeline duration; Scroll-driven Animations currentTime as a percentage CSSUnitValue). The probe read endTime '100%' and Number.isFinite false, so the test never finishes it and reads it at the current scroll position. A scroll-driven (scroll(root)) padding growth on both tags, filled both ways, passed all 12 in 3 of 3 runs. The page shows 12px padding at the top and a larger padding once scrolled, at both 1280x1000 and 800x800. A scroll-driven scale on the tags failed 3 of 3 through the strict running-animation branch, so the gap affects only box properties. (c) The first example, 'a paused, delayed or very long animation that does not hold its effect after it ends', leaves out the original owner-accepted cl5 case. That case is a very long or paused animation that does hold its effect, with an identity end. A 100000s linear forwards-filled animation on both tags from a reduced scale to identity passed all 12 in 3 of 3 runs and is drawn reduced at every sample. The loop-8 text named this case ('ends at the expected values'); the loop-9 qualifier drops it. The examples are introduced as non-exhaustive, so (c) is a note only. Why low and not higher: every case is covered by the general sentence 'Any animation that changes the drawn size at some other moment can therefore go undetected', and README task 11 Outcome (line 141) forbids all of them for learners. Only maintainer and evidence wording is affected, and the detection itself falls inside the owner's option A residual. No detection change is asked for. Like cl8-sme-001, this is a precision gap in a gloss, not an unnamed category of passing wrong pages.

evidence.section: 4.9.1 Calculating the directed progress (current direction is reverse for playback direction reverse and alternates per iteration for alternate, so the end of the final iteration is not always the last keyframe)
Timelines: timeline duration (a non-monotonic, e.g. scroll, timeline is a progress-based timeline whose timeline duration is 100%, and timing is converted to proportions)
ScrollTimeline and ViewTimeline interfaces: currentTime is the scroll progress as a percentage CSSUnitValue

findings.recommendation: Wording only, in lab.json notes and the next solved-run record's not-covered list, with no test, README or starter change and no new enumeration. Change three phrases. 'the finite animations' becomes 'the finite time-based animations'. '(its last keyframe if it fills forwards, otherwise its unanimated values)' becomes '(its end value if it fills forwards, otherwise its unanimated values)'. 'and it reads every other animation, on any element, as it is at that moment' becomes 'and it reads every other animation, including scroll-driven ones, on any element, as it is at that moment'. In the first example, drop the qualifier 'that does not hold its effect after it ends', or replace it with 'whatever it holds at its end'.

items.note: Checked lab.json line 87 at 598e61a2 and the record's variantRuns at 8135e3b5. Part (a), the scope of finishing: the text now says the test finishes animations only on the checklist and the two tags and reads every other animation, on any element, as it is at that moment, and it gives 'any animation on an element around the checklist' as an example. Probe: a delayed forwards-filled reduced scale on .page passed all 12 in 3 of 3 runs, as now described. Part (b), the held end: the text now says a forwards fill holds its end and any other fill leaves the unanimated values. Probe: a paused backwards-filled reduced-scale hold on both tags passed all 12 in 3 of 3, and the same hold filled both ways failed task 11 in 3 of 3, both as described. The recommended wording was adopted. The remaining 'last keyframe' and scroll-driven imprecision is a new, separate gloss issue, raised as cl9-sme-001.

The record's not-covered list (line 49 at 8135e3b5) and lab.json line 87 no longer limit the residual to width or padding. They state the general rule that any animation changing the drawn size at another moment can go undetected. The examples cover paused, delayed or very long animations, endless ones resting at none, a pulsing checklist zoom, animations on elements around the checklist, and animated custom properties, which are the four cl7 categories. Test bytes are identical to 80eff5af (git diff --quiet on the lab's tests, starter, README and expected, and on the-box-model topic.json), so the cl7 behaviour is unchanged. Of the cl7 cases I re-ran only the ancestor and paused ones, under cl8-sme-001; the others are cited from unchanged code. See cl9-sme-001(c) for one example qualifier that now leaves out the cl5 identity-end case.

The narrower fix is in place at lines 157-159: while any animation on the element is not finished, only the literal none and zoom 1 count as unscaled. Each of these failed task 11 and no other task in 3 of 3 runs on the completed work: an endless alternating scale from 1 on both tags, an endless 4s linear rotate spin from 0deg on both tags, and an endless scale pulse from 1 on .site-aside. Before loop 7 these passed in most runs. The width and padding part of the finding is the owner's option A residual and is now stated in lab.json and the record ('an endless animation (for example one changing a width or padding ...)'). The solved-run record no longer claims that every endless animation is caught.

Animations are no longer removed. Lines 140-144 finish only animations with a finite end time on the checklist and the tags, and transitions are set to none only while measuring and restored at lines 238-243. The three cl4 variants each failed task 11 and no other task in 3 of 3 runs on the completed work: (a) a short forwards-filled animation holding .pack-tag-day at another width, (b) an infinite transform-scale animation on both tags, and (c) a short forwards-filled animation holding .pack-tag-overnight at a larger padding. The unmodified completed work passed all 12 in 3 of 3.
